name: Chicken thighs
notes: Cheap and forgiving; at long pressure times expect shredded texture.

name: Chicken drumsticks
notes: Bone-in; contributes more broth body than thighs.

name: Chicken feet
notes: Stock builder, not a substantial meat portion.

name: Beef short ribs
notes: Very rich; pair with lighter vegetables and acid.

name: Beef shank
notes: Marrow and connective tissue enrich the liquid.

name: Pork shoulder
notes: Better timing match for dried beans than chicken.

name: Pork stewing cubes
notes: Timing depends on cut and leanness.

name: Smoked turkey leg
notes: Lighter smoked alternative to ham hock.

name: Turkey neck
notes: Good-value broth meat; watch small bones.

name: Pork neck bones
notes: Budget broth option; watch bone fragments.

name: Smoked sausage
notes: A small amount can season the whole pot.

name: Bacon
notes: Render first; reserve some for topping if desired.

name: Garlic
notes: Add after onion; do not scorch.

name: Water
notes: Neutral base; needs other flavor builders.

name: Red wine
notes: Best with dark meats; can overpower delicate chicken builds.

name: Beer
notes: Dark beer can contribute substantial bitterness.

name: Celery root
notes: Can partly dissolve and thicken broth.

name: Butternut squash
notes: Usually dissolves in a long cook.

name: Cabbage
notes: Move to simmer_after if you want more texture.

name: Dried black beans
notes: Old beans may need soaking and longer cooking.

name: Red lentils (simmer after)
notes: Useful post-opening correction knob; good for thickening a thin broth.

name: Green lentils
notes: Hold shape better than red lentils.

name: Split peas
notes: Break down into a velvety base.

name: Miso
notes: Dissolve in hot broth after pressure cooking.

name: Croutons
notes: Add only at serving; best in soupier builds.

name: Salt
notes: Dosage-dependent; do not score as an ingredient-level balance axis.

name: Coconut milk
notes: Light coconut milk holds up to pressure; stir thicker coconut cream in near the end to avoid splitting.

name: Peanut butter
notes: Stir in near the end to enrich and thicken; thin with broth to prevent clumping.

name: Fresh chile
notes: Adjust amount to taste; remove seeds for less heat.

name: Mint
notes: Add at the end; brightens rich or bean-heavy builds.
